questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: A solution of a metal ion when treated with KI gives a red precipitate which dissolves in excess KI to give a colourless solution. Moreover, the solution of metal ion on treatment with a solution of cobalt (II) thiocyanate gives rise to a deep blue crystalline precipitate. The metal ion is
questions.solution:
When a solution of a Hg2+ is treated with KI a red precipitate of (HgI2) is obtained which dissolves in excess KI to give a colourless solution (HgI4)2- . When the solution of Hg2+ is treated with a solution of cobalt (II) thiocyanate a deep blue crystalline precipitate of Hg(SCN)2 is formed. The reactions are as follows
Hg2++2I–→HgI2
HgI2(excess)+2I–→[HgI4]2–Soluble
Hg 2+ +Co (SCN) 2 → Hg (SCN) 2 Blue crystal line ppt.

Here other ion Pb2+ , Hg2+ and Co2+ do not give precipitates formed in these reactions.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: 0.45 gm of an organic compound gave on combustion 0.792 gm of CO<sub>2</sub> and 0.324 gm of water. 0.24 gm of the same substance was Kjeldahlised and the ammonia liberated was absorbed in 50.0 ml of M/8 H<sub>2</sub>SO<sub>4</sub>. The excess acid required 77.0 ml of N/10 NaOH for complete neutralisation. Calculate the empirical formula of the compound.
questions.solution:
Calculation of the percentage composition :

i)  Percentage of carbon

= 1 2 4 4 × Mass of CO 2 Produced Mass of substance taken × 1 0 0

= 1 2 4 4 × 0 . 7 9 2 0 . 4 5 × 1 0 0 = 4 8 . 0

ii)  Percentage of hydrogen

= 2 1 8 × Mass of H 2 O produced Mass of substance taken × 1 0 0

= 2 1 8 × 0 . 3 2 4 0 . 4 5 × 1 0 0 = 8 . 0

iii)  Percentage of nitrogen

mEq. of H2SO4 = 5 0 × M 8 × 2 = 1 2 . 5

mEq. of NaOH = 7 2 × 1 1 0 × 1 = 7 . 7

Excess of H2SO4 used to neutralise ammonia

= 12.5 - 7.7 = 4.8

Percentage of N2 = 1 . 4 × 4 . 8 0 . 2 4 = 2 8 . 0 %

iv)  Percentage of oxygen = 100 - (percentage of C + percentage of H + percentage of N) = 100 - (48.0 + 8.0 + 28.0) = 16.0.

b.  Calculation of empirical formula :

 
Element Percentage Atomic mass number of atoms Relative number of atoms Simlpest atomic ratio Simplest whole number atomic ratio
Carbon 48.8 12 4 8 . 0 1 2 = 4 4 1 = 4 4
Hydrogen 8.0 1 8 . 0 1 = 8 8 . 0 1 = 8 8
Nitrogen 28.0 14 2 8 . 0 1 4 = 2 2 1 = 2 2
Oxygen 16.0 16 1 6 . 0 1 6 = 1 1 1 = 1 1


Hence, the empirical formula of the compound is C4H8N2O.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
The correct match between item 'I' and item 'II' is
Item I (Compound) Item II (Reagent)
(1) Lysine (P) 1-naphthol
(2) Furfural (Q) ninhydrin
(3) Isopropyl alcohol (R) KMnO4
(4) Vinyl benzene (Styrene) (S) Ceric ammonium Nitrate
questions.solution:
Lysine (amino acid) can be tested by ninhydrin as ninhydrin test is used for testing amino acids.
Furfural can be tested by 1-naphthol.
Isopropyl alcohol can be tested by Ceric ammonium nitrate which is a yellow reagent and on reaction with alcohol changes to red.
Vinyl benzene (Styrene) can be tested by KMnO4 as styrene decolourises alk. KMnO4 due to presence of unsaturation (double bond).
